shapes.dataIs: A row set the user EDITS: a position book, a contact list, an inventory. The rows are the answer, not the raw material.
shapes.shape: `.dt` datatable: sortable columns, inline cell editing, saved views in the foot, column groups, row drills to a `datarow` panel.
shapes.proves: the framework ships a real spreadsheet, not a read-only listing
shapes.antiPattern: Do NOT reach here first. A grid is correct only when the user edits rows. If the user's question is 'what happened' or 'where did we land', pick stream or walk.

shapes.dataIs: Events in time, newest or oldest first, each carrying a few typed facts: orders, deploys, webhook deliveries, audit entries, transactions.
shapes.shape: One CSS-grid row per event with the discriminating field as a coloured 14px chip (side, verb, level), monospace tabular figures, and voided rows struck through at 45% opacity. Low-value columns drop at `@container` breakpoints.
shapes.proves: a dense event log stays readable at any panel width without a horizontal scrollbar
shapes.antiPattern: Not a grid: the user reads a stream top to bottom, never sorts it by column.

shapes.dataIs: Entities compared by MAGNITUDE, each carrying a state: accounts by balance, regions by revenue, services by cost, tenants by seat count.
shapes.shape: One row per entity: a 7px state dot, the name, a proportional bar sized against the set's own maximum, the figure right-aligned tabular, and a signed tail for anything pending. The bar is a div, never a chart.
shapes.proves: comparison and state in one glance, with zero chart dependency
shapes.antiPattern: Do not add a pie chart. The bar IS the comparison.

shapes.dataIs: A computation that DESCENDS to a result: a P&L to EBITDA, a funnel to conversion, a bill to a total, a score to a grade.
shapes.shape: One row per term with sub-terms indented and totals ruled top and bottom. Two overlaid bars: the plan outlined with `--rule-3` (a filled ghost vanishes in dark), the actual filled. The delta colours from MEANING, not sign.
shapes.proves: a derived result shows its own arithmetic, so the number is auditable in place
shapes.antiPattern: Never colour a delta from its raw sign. A cost under plan is favourable while its delta is negative: `good = isCost ? delta < 0 : delta > 0`.

shapes.dataIs: A quantity consumed over time with a breakdown: API spend, storage, seats, credits, bandwidth.
shapes.shape: A range segmented control, three stat tiles, an inline `svg` bar series with `preserveAspectRatio="none"` and the latest bar accented, then a by-dimension breakdown as proportional rows.
shapes.proves: time series plus breakdown in one panel, still no chart library
shapes.antiPattern: Do not import a charting package for eight bars.

shapes.dataIs: Consumption against a CEILING the user set: spend limits, rate limits, plan allowances.
shapes.shape: One line per limit: the label, a track filled to the consumed fraction, the ceiling as an editable field, and the projected breach date when the trend crosses it.
shapes.proves: a settable ceiling and its consumption are the same object, not a settings page plus a dashboard
shapes.antiPattern: Do not split the limit into a settings screen and its usage into a chart screen.

shapes.dataIs: A fleet of things that are up or down: services, integrations, regions, workers, jobs.
shapes.shape: One row per service: a state dot, the name, the current latency or figure, and a compact 30-slot uptime strip. Incidents drill to their own panel.
shapes.proves: a status page is a panel, and every incident is one click deeper without leaving it
shapes.antiPattern: Do not put a modal on an incident. It drills right.

shapes.dataIs: Append-only lines carrying a level: application logs, job runs, delivery attempts, moderation events.
shapes.shape: Monospace lines with the level as a `.pf-pill`, the message truncated with the full text on the row's panel, filters as foot segments, and the line drills to a detail panel with the payload.
shapes.proves: a log viewer needs no separate detail page: the line opens right
shapes.antiPattern: Do not expand rows in place. Expansion loses the list; a drill keeps both.

shapes.dataIs: A session the user drives by typing: a terminal, a REPL, a query console, an agent run.
shapes.shape: A monospace scrollback pinned to the bottom, and the prompt IS THE FOOT. The panel has no other action zone, which is exactly the foot law paying off.
shapes.proves: the foot is a composer, not just a button bar
shapes.antiPattern: Do not put the input inside the body. The foot is the single action zone.

shapes.dataIs: A turn-taking conversation: a chat, a support ticket, a review thread, a comment stream.
shapes.shape: Alternating message blocks with the role as the only chrome, attachments as chips, a typing indicator, and the composer in the foot with its attachment rail.
shapes.proves: a chat surface inherits the same panel skeleton as a table
shapes.antiPattern: Do not build a floating chat widget. It is a panel like everything else.

shapes.dataIs: A configuration OBJECT with sections: a prompt spec, a webhook, a pipeline step, a form definition, a policy.
shapes.shape: Stacked labelled sections, each a titled group of tokenized fields, with variables as removable chips and a live preview. The title IS the first field (no form card).
shapes.proves: a settings surface needs no form card: the panel is the form
shapes.antiPattern: Never wrap fields in a card with its own heading. That is the AxF5 violation.

shapes.dataIs: Mutually exclusive choices with consequences: retention policy, visibility, plan tier, region.
shapes.shape: Radio rows where the CONSEQUENCE is the body text, not a tooltip, plus a hint line stating what changes when the choice changes.
shapes.proves: a policy screen states its own blast radius inline
shapes.antiPattern: Do not hide the consequence behind an info icon.

shapes.dataIs: Credentials: API keys, tokens, signing secrets, certificates.
shapes.shape: Masked rows with the prefix visible, a REVEAL-ONCE dialog at creation (the secret never reappears), roll and revoke as row actions, last-used and scope as columns.
shapes.proves: the reveal-once contract is a first-class panel behaviour
shapes.antiPattern: Never re-show a secret after creation, and never put it in a URL.

shapes.dataIs: People with roles: team members, permissions, invitations, assignees.
shapes.shape: Avatar rows with the role as an inline editable select, pending invitations distinguished, and the owner guarded from demotion. The invite composer lives in the foot.
shapes.proves: the permission matrix and the invite flow are one panel
shapes.antiPattern: Do not open an invite modal.

shapes.dataIs: Visual artifacts: generated images, uploads, screenshots, thumbnails, brand assets.
shapes.shape: A density-switchable grid of tiles, each drilling to its own panel with the prompt, the parameters and the actions. Lazy below the fold.
shapes.proves: a media grid and its detail live side by side instead of a lightbox
shapes.antiPattern: Do not use a lightbox. A lightbox is a modal wearing a costume.

shapes.dataIs: A launcher: an entry surface that routes to the real work, a home, a workspace picker.
shapes.shape: Large cards, each naming a destination and its live count, opening the destination to the right rather than replacing the view.
shapes.proves: even a home screen keeps its parent on stage
shapes.antiPattern: Do not make the hub a route that unmounts everything.

shapes.dataIs: Items moving through PHASES: a pipeline, a kanban, a review queue, an editorial calendar.
shapes.shape: Columns as phase bands driven by `colGroups`, drag between columns writing the phase field, and the card drilling to the item's panel.
shapes.proves: the board is a VIEW of the same collection as the table, not a second data model
shapes.antiPattern: Never build a board on its own data. It is a view type on the collection.

shapes.dataIs: One object's fields: a contact, an account, a deal, a document's metadata.
shapes.shape: Label and value rows where the value is directly editable, related collections as drillable counts, and the activity trail below. The title is the object's name and is editable in the bar.
shapes.proves: an entity detail is a panel with a parent still visible, so context never breaks
shapes.antiPattern: Do not open an entity in a modal or a new route.

shapes.dataIs: A graph: an architecture, a flow, a dependency map, an org chart.
shapes.shape: Nodes and edges on a pannable canvas, a node click drilling to its inspector panel, an edge click to the edge inspector.
shapes.proves: a spatial surface and a structured inspector coexist without a sidebar
shapes.antiPattern: Do not put node properties in a floating overlay.

shapes.dataIs: Weighted criteria that roll to a decision: a diligence rubric, a vendor evaluation, a risk score, a grading sheet.
shapes.shape: Criteria grouped into bands, each row carrying its weight, a DISCRETE dot rail for the score (not a slider: the scale is ordinal), and the evidence sentence beside it. The total and the verdict band are DERIVED from the rows, never stored next to them. A segmented control switches between an automated pass and the human's own.
shapes.proves: a judgement surface where the arithmetic is visible, so the score can be argued with
shapes.antiPattern: Do not store the total. A stored total drifts from its criteria on the first edit, and then nobody knows which is true.

shapes.dataIs: Two sets that should pair up but do not yet: invoices against bank lines, orders against shipments, records against a merge candidate, duplicates.
shapes.shape: Two columns facing each other with the proposed pairing between them, carrying a CONFIDENCE whose visual weight scales with its value, the reason for the proposal stated in words below, and accept/reject per pair. The discrepancy is shown on the value itself, not hidden in a tooltip.
shapes.proves: a human-in-the-loop decision surface: the machine proposes with its reasoning exposed, the human disposes per row
shapes.antiPattern: Do not auto-apply high confidence matches silently, and do not show a confidence without the reason that produced it.

shapes.dataIs: One total split by an ownership key: a capital call by commitment, a cost by cost centre, a bonus pool by headcount, a quota by territory.
shapes.shape: One row per participant: a state dot for their standing on the PREVIOUS round, the name, their share as a percentage, a bar proportional to their slice, and the amount. The individual amounts are computed from the share, so they always sum to the total.
shapes.proves: a derived split that cannot fail to reconcile, with each participant's history carried on the same line
shapes.antiPattern: Do not let a user type individual amounts beside a total. Compute them, or the two disagree.

shapes.dataIs: An ordered set of checks where one failure stops the thing: a kill check, a deploy gate, a compliance screen, a pre-flight, an eligibility test.
shapes.shape: The VERDICT FIRST, in a band coloured by outcome and stating the reason in one line, then the gates that produced it. Each gate shows its mark, whether it is blocking, and its evidence. A blocking failure is visually distinct from an unanswered question.
shapes.proves: a decision surface that leads with the answer instead of making the reader reconstruct it from a list
shapes.antiPattern: Do not render a gate as a plain checklist. A checklist with one fatal item and one cosmetic item treats them alike.

shapes.dataIs: Recurring commitments in a period: a meeting rhythm, an on-call rota, a publishing calendar, a maintenance window schedule.
shapes.shape: The period as a GRID of its units, each holding its commitments as small blocks with the time, what and who, and a left border keyed to the kind. An empty unit says so. The shape makes the week's WEIGHT visible without counting.
shapes.proves: a schedule read as a shape rather than a list, so imbalance is seen rather than computed
shapes.antiPattern: Do not render a recurring schedule as a sorted list of instances. The whole value is the distribution.

shapes.dataIs: The front door: a sign in surface, a workspace picker, an invitation acceptance, any screen that ROUTES a person into the product.
shapes.shape: The SAME panel component as everything behind it, at the registry M width: bar 44 with the product mark, body 18/18/16 carrying an eyebrow, a name, one paragraph and the sign in method, foot 7/14 with exactly ONE primary and a quiet link to the sibling entrance. Several entrances differ ONLY in the eyebrow, the copy, the method and the refusal set.
shapes.proves: the panel grammar reaches the front door, so a product has one component from sign in to the deepest drill
shapes.antiPattern: A landing page ROUTES AND BRANDS, it never authorises. Capabilities are the only gate and visibility config can only hide. Do not build a second identity instance per entrance: one human would then hold two subjects and the whole identity argument dies quietly.

shapes.dataIs: A denied state: no session, a session with no record, a suspended account, a session with no surface, or a legitimate ambiguity the product must not resolve for the user.
shapes.shape: One row per refusal, each opening to what it ENFORCES, what it LEAKS and the TRAP that makes it tempting to build wrong, plus the exact sentence shown and the exit action. The sentence is the artefact: it is quoted, not paraphrased.
shapes.proves: denial is a designed state with a contract, not an afterthought behind a 403
shapes.antiPattern: A denied element renders its empty expression or NOTHING. Never a hidden but present control, never a greyed control whose tooltip names the capability it wants, never a masked value, never a count that includes rows the reader cannot see. Never disclose whether an account exists, and never name the missing membership: that answer describes your business.
